# Subscribe to premium in the app

## Problem Statement

Existing free users who track habits on two or more devices lose their streaks, because the free app keeps habits on one phone only. In the last quarter 1,200 support requests asked for sync between devices. The vision offers sync as part of a paid premium plan, but premium does not exist yet, so a free user who wants it has no way to get it inside the app. This plan lets a free user see premium's monthly price and subscribe to premium from inside the app without contacting support, and makes the app recognise who is premium so nobody pays twice.

This plan does not decide the monthly price. The original stub asked for the price to be decided here, but pricing is the owner's business decision. It is made in the Product Loop, outside the CTOC technical pipeline, and has been raised with the owner in this plan's status file. Every criterion below holds for whatever price the owner sets.

## Business Alignment

**Job to Be Done:** When I track my habits on two or more devices and want the same habits and streaks on all of them, I want to subscribe to premium from inside the app, so I can get sync without contacting support.

**Impact Map:**
- **Goal:** Free users on more than one device can get premium (and with it, sync) on their own. This traces to the vision's first success criterion: "A free user can subscribe to premium from inside the app without contacting support." Today that need shows up as support requests (1,200 last quarter).
- **Actor:** An existing free user of the habit tracker who uses it on two or more devices (the vision's target audience).
- **Impact:** The actor subscribes inside the app instead of filing a support request. This can be observed as subscriptions completed in the app with no support contact.
- **Deliverable:** A premium offer inside the app that shows the monthly price, a subscribe flow with clear success and failure outcomes, and recognition of an active subscription so premium is never sold twice to the same account.

**Alignment checks:**
1. Goal traces to the vision's problem statement: YES. The vision offers sync "as part of a paid premium plan that a user subscribes to from inside the app."
2. Actor is in the vision's target audience: YES. It is the same audience: free users on two or more devices.
3. Impact is observable: YES. A completed subscription is visible, with no support contact needed.
4. Deliverable covers one functional area: YES. It covers subscribing and premium status only. Sync is excluded (see Out of Scope).

**Sibling overlap check:** `Glob plans/functional/habit-tracker-premium-*.md` matched 1 file (this one). There is no sibling stub, so there is no overlap.

## User Stories

**As a** free user who tracks habits on two or more devices, **I want** to see what premium adds and what it costs per month and then subscribe from inside the app, **so that** I get premium without contacting support.

**As a** user who has paid for premium, **I want** the app to recognise my active subscription on every device where I sign in to my account, **so that** I am never asked or charged to pay for premium twice.

## Acceptance Criteria

Story 1: subscribe from inside the app

- [ ] **Scenario: Free user sees what premium adds and its monthly price before paying**
  Given a free user on a device with a network connection
  When they open the premium offer from inside the app
  Then they see that premium adds sync of their habits and streaks between their devices
  And they see the monthly price the owner has set, before any payment is requested

- [ ] **Scenario: Free user subscribes successfully**
  Given a free user viewing the premium offer
  When they confirm the subscription and the payment succeeds
  Then within 5 seconds of the payment succeeding they see a confirmation that premium is active
  And they are charged the monthly price shown on the offer, and no other amount

- [ ] **Scenario: Payment is declined**
  Given a free user viewing the premium offer
  When they confirm the subscription and the payment is declined
  Then they see a message that the payment did not go through and that they have not been charged
  And they are still a free user, with every habit and streak on the device unchanged
  And they can try to subscribe again from the same screen

- [ ] **Scenario: Free user backs out before paying**
  Given a free user viewing the premium offer
  When they close the offer or cancel the payment step without confirming
  Then they are not charged
  And they return to the screen they came from, still a free user, with their habits unchanged

- [ ] **Scenario: No network connection**
  Given a free user whose device has no network connection
  When they try to subscribe to premium
  Then they see a message that subscribing needs a network connection
  And they are not charged and are still a free user

Story 2: an active subscription is recognised, so premium is never paid for twice

- [ ] **Scenario: Premium user is not offered premium again**
  Given a user whose premium subscription is active
  When they open the place in the app where premium is offered
  Then they see that premium is active, and no option to subscribe is shown

- [ ] **Scenario: Repeated confirmation charges once**
  Given a free user viewing the premium offer
  When they confirm the subscription a second time before the first confirmation has completed
  Then they are charged the monthly price once
  And they hold one premium subscription

- [ ] **Scenario: Payment succeeded but the app closed before the confirmation**
  Given a user whose payment for premium succeeded while the app closed before showing the confirmation
  When they open the app again with a network connection
  Then the app shows them as premium
  And no option to subscribe is shown

- [ ] **Scenario: Premium is recognised on a second device**
  Given a user who subscribed to premium on one device
  When they sign in to the same account on a second device that has a network connection
  Then the second device shows them as premium
  And no option to subscribe is shown, and they are not charged again

- [ ] **Scenario: Subscription ends without renewal**
  Given a premium user whose subscription has ended without renewal
  When they next open the app with a network connection
  Then the app shows them as a free user and offers premium again
  And no habit or streak is removed from the device they are using

## Scope

### In Scope
- A premium offer inside the app that shows what premium adds and the monthly price the owner has set, before any payment is requested (Scenario: Free user sees what premium adds and its monthly price before paying)
- Subscribing to premium monthly from inside the app, with a confirmation that premium is active (Scenario: Free user subscribes successfully)
- Failed, abandoned and offline attempts: no charge, the user stays free, and habits are untouched (Scenarios: Payment is declined; Free user backs out before paying; No network connection)
- Recognising an active subscription so premium is never offered or charged twice. This covers the same device, a repeated confirmation, and a confirmation the user missed (Scenarios: Premium user is not offered premium again; Repeated confirmation charges once; Payment succeeded but the app closed before the confirmation)
- Recognising premium on a second device signed in to the same account (Scenario: Premium is recognised on a second device)
- Returning the user to free when the subscription ends (Scenario: Subscription ends without renewal)

### Out of Scope
- **Deciding the monthly price.** The original stub asked for it to be decided here. It is the owner's business decision, made in the Product Loop outside the CTOC technical pipeline, and it has been raised with the owner in this plan's status file. This plan works for any price the owner sets.
- **Syncing habits and streaks between devices.** This is in the vision's scope and is its second success criterion, but no functional plan covers it: `Glob plans/functional/habit-tracker-premium-*.md` matched only this file. The owner decides where that work lives and when it is built.
- **What happens to synced habits when premium ends.** This belongs with the sync work above, which has no plan yet.
- **Team or family plans.** The vision excludes them.
- **The web version of the app.** The vision excludes it, so subscribing happens in the phone and tablet app only.
- **Managing or cancelling a subscription from inside the app, free trials, discounts, and billing periods other than monthly.** The stub names a monthly subscription only, and none of these appears in the vision or in any stub. Whether any of them is wanted is the owner's decision.

## Risks

### Technical Risks
- **Platform payment rules are unknown.** The vision names neither the platforms the app ships on nor a payment route. Those platforms decide which payment route an in-app subscription may use, and the rules that route imposes on price display, renewal and cancellation. Those rules were not researched for this plan.
  - Likelihood: HIGH
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Research the in-app subscription rules of each target platform before the implementation plan fixes the payment route. CTO Chief can dispatch deepthink-researcher for this.
- **The payment confirmation can arrive late, or after the app has closed.** A user who paid could then be shown as free and pay again.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Test the path where the app closes between payment and confirmation (Scenario: Payment succeeded but the app closed before the confirmation) and the repeated-confirmation path before release.

### Business Risks
- **No monthly price has been set.** Without a price the offer cannot show one, and no user can subscribe. This blocks the feature from going live; it does not block building it.
  - Likelihood: HIGH (no price had been decided when this plan was refined)
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Raise the price decision with the owner (done in this plan's status file). Build against the price as a value the owner supplies, never as a number chosen by the pipeline.
- **Premium could be sold before sync exists.** Sync is the only premium benefit the vision names, and no functional plan for it exists. A subscriber could pay for a benefit they do not get.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM. It depends on the build order the owner chooses.
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Show the owner at Gate 1 that the sync work has no functional plan, so the owner decides how this plan and the sync work are ordered.

### Dependency Risks
- **Sign-in to an account is assumed but not confirmed.** Recognising premium on a second device needs users to sign in to an account. The vision assumes this ("every device they sign in on"), but this project has no app source in which to confirm that accounts exist: `Glob {src,docs,skills}/**/*` matched 0 files.
  - Likelihood: MEDIUM
  - Impact: HIGH
  - Mitigation: Confirm in the app's code, during implementation planning, whether users sign in to an account. If they do not, raise it with the owner before building Scenario: Premium is recognised on a second device.

## Priority

**Priority: HIGH** (Score: 8/9)
- Dependency: MEDIUM (2). No other stub exists, so no stub depends on this one and this one depends on none. The vision's sync work will need this plan's premium status to know who gets sync, but it has no plan yet.
- Business Impact: HIGH (3). Subscribing in the app is the vision's first success criterion, and it is how premium, and with it sync, reaches users at all.
- Technical Risk: HIGH (3). Payment is an external integration whose route and rules are not yet known (see Technical Risks).
